fresh_checks.check: The connected compact setup allows arbitrary smooth big θ; bounded mass and positive lower reference volume supply a finite positive relative mass interval.
The main theorem requires nonzero finite non-pluripolar data and distinguishes exponential potential uniqueness from exponent-zero scalar uniqueness.
Background and singularity monotonicity imply positive lower volume of the auxiliary Hermitian metric from the positive reference volume.
Fixed-dominator continuity checks finite-rooftop, stretching and positive lower mass in the arbitrary background before reusing the semipositive proof.
Disjoint first-contact pieces give fixed-measure rooftop domination without an obstacle-count factor; prefix and tail stretches supply all class conditions.
Weighted extended lower semicontinuity followed by big-relative zero domination identifies the lower-tail limit; raw fixed-measure tails identify the undamped limit.
The first-moment proof chooses an ordinary-type representative with mass greater than M-ℓ/2 and translates it below the reference.
The maximum measure estimate includes the equality set in the reference contact part and retains the defect M-μw'(X).
Splitting the rooftop mass at depth s gives K/s plus the fixed finite tail and the chosen mass defect; successive limits exclude collapse.
If a limiting stretch collapsed, normalized compactness would otherwise produce a genuine competitor; the same mass-defect contradiction proves all stretches genuine.
The resulting convex volume bound recovers full upper volume as b tends to infinity; the one-sided moment version uses a genuine rooftop below both obstacles.
Self-measure convergence uses summable absolute errors on disjoint rooftop contacts; the one-sided first-moment criterion produces genuine tail envelopes in the class.
Bounded truncated difference weights converge in capacity after discarding deep sublevels; zero domination and upper/lower squeezing prove capacity convergence.
The minimal-reference concave obstacle is of ordinary minimal type because its input difference is bounded.
The inverse concave transformation is convex with derivative at most one; local bounded positivity and analytic removability justify its global θ-potential.
Ordered contact and the inverse derivative give the exact χ'^n envelope measure bound, with the analytic polar complement ignored.
In the higher-moment proof the essential tail depth T is finite; zero domination upgrades the measure-tail bound to pointwise order.
The tail-dependent derivative is locally bounded on [0,T-s], and the integrable continuation gives Tonelli's uniform bound 3 max(1,MV).
Chebyshev and two integrations yield W_s(t)≥c(1+B)^(-1/N)t^(1+1/(2N)), with the bounded initial interval treated separately.
N=2n+1 makes the Cauchy–Schwarz exponent exactly one half; positive lower mass bounds the envelope supremum by CB.
Finite Aθ controls the normalized envelope integral; the r-moment follows from layer cake with 1<r<1+1/(2N).
Uniform integrability includes the fixed L1 term -V and does not assert an Lr bound for V itself.
Smoothed-measure continuity first gives relative class membership by first moments, then L1 of the original measure by uniform integrability and larger-Hermitian truncations.
The smoothing lemma turns that L1 convergence into a self-measure error; the C'/T tail estimate and bounded mass identify the raw weak limit.
For finite-Aθ probability data, normalized scalars lie in [ℓV,MV]; Jensen bounds exponential normalization above and positive mass bounds it below.
The bounded-carrier density decomposition gives finite Aθ for each bounded truncation; fixed finite domination passes arbitrary normalized and exponential data to the minimal class.
Metric positive volume plus a strict θ-potential gives positive minimal-reference lower volume by addition of the residual positive current.
The cross-class rooftop uses a small reference stretch and an upper-class stretch to construct one convex competitor below both obstacles.
As the small stretch tends to one its upper volume recovers the lower reference volume; upward stability handles a general upper-class potential after translation.
Relative projection has a uniform model-plus-supremum bound; the increasing canonical limit stays in the class and contact support controls its measure.
Projecting a minimal exponential solution gives a weighted measure below the datum; its positive unweighted lower mass ensures this weighted measure is nonzero.
Varying-model closure extracts monotone model lower bounds with volume at least δ/2 and volume convergence to the limiting reference.
The projected auxiliary obstacle controls contact pieces where the restricted domination hypothesis applies; ν+μχ is one fixed finite dominator.
The minimum exponential test has a positive almost-everywhere lower reference; it prevents finite-rooftop collapse uniformly in the last obstacle.
Fixed-class dominated continuity passes each finite rooftop tail to its lower model; monotonicity of upper volumes recovers the limiting relative class.
Full domination additionally gives lower-tail equality by weighted lower semicontinuity and zero domination, capacity squeezing and uniformly vanishing raw tails.
The weighted common-bound lemma needs no relative-class claim for its finite roofs; the tail envelopes acquire class membership from the common lower bound and limiting singularity order.
The truncated addition limit keeps retained truncation levels, estimates errors outside the strict locality sets by exponential decay and uses finite fixed input measures.
A common-lower-potential cutoff identifies the addition equation using a signed bounded-product expansion in a dominating Hermitian background before removing the cutoff.
Exponent scaling multiplies backgrounds and potentials by λ and measures by λ^n; common translation preserves the difference-weighted addition equation.
Ordinary-minimal addition truncates weights only, uses an average-minus-D subsolution and obtains a fixed finite dominator before passing to the equation.
The input comparison is made after the limiting addition equation; the weight-truncated equations alone do not supply that order.
Two same-ordinary-type inputs have a common lower bound despite minimal-type approximants; the limiting lemma explicitly permits this change of type.
For one ordinary-type input, the Q2 contact coefficient cancels at δ=n log 2; disjoint finite roofs and t exp(-t/2) bound the reference first moment.
For a bounded-carrier input, normalized carrier integrability supplies its moment, while one extra rooftop gives the fixed dominator μu+2^n μv and a common lower envelope after extraction.
The model-equation maximum is attained using fixed domination, weak limits of weighted measures and continuous approximation in L1 of the dominating datum.
A nonzero remaining deficit has a projected supersolution with bounded-carrier measure; weighted addition contradicts maximal weighted mass.
Monotone density truncation passes general prescribed data to the class; general exponent scales the datum by λ^n and uniqueness uses two-way exponential order.
At exponent 1/j, u1+(j-1)sup u1 gives the upper scalar bound; lower mass and normalized exponential integrability yield a positive scalar in [ℓ/μX,M/μX].
Varying-model equations obtain a fixed dominator by summable L1 density errors; uniqueness gives whole-sequence convergence only for a positive exponent.
Zero-exponent varying equations give scalar and total-variation convergence plus the equation of every potential cluster, without claiming unique potential convergence.
Arbitrary weighted addition prevents collapse by a first moment before input comparison; a rooftop of the limit and inputs localizes the signed-product passage, then strict domination proves a≤u,v.
Injectivity of the weighted measure map proves associativity, commutativity, translation covariance and the self-addition shift even for infinite weighted total mass.
The general-model concave transform uses decreasing local bounded pair truncations and canonical overlap limits rather than assuming local boundedness off an analytic pole set.
The finite m>2n+1 datum moment bounds the transformed envelope supremum and W^m integral independently of the stopping depth S.
The differential inequality has γ<1 and κ>1; integrating W^(1-κ) bounds every S<T uniformly and zero domination converts the finite depth to bounded difference.
Uniform exponential integrability plus Hölder gives every finite datum moment for nonzero Lp data; the domination is applied after normalizing the actual relative solution.
